description.text: As used herein, “Wayfair,” “the company,” “we,” “us,” “our” and similar terms refer to Wayfair Inc. and its subsidiaries, unless the context indicates otherwise. Wayfair is the destination for all things home. Through our e-commerce platform, we offer customers visually inspired browsing, compelling merchandising, easy product discovery and attractive prices. We are focused on bringing our customers an experience that is at the forefront of shopping for the home online. Our customers span a wide range of demographics, with annual household incomes typically ranging from $25,000 to over $250,000, and also include businesses, from small startups to global enterprises. Our selections of furniture, décor, housewares and home improvement products appeal to our customers’ different tastes, styles, purchasing goals and budgets when shopping for their homes and businesses. To meet our customers where they are, we offer a family of brands, both online and through physical retail stores, each with a unique identity that offers a tailored shopping experience and rich product selection to a different target audience: •Wayfair: Every style. Every home. •AllModern: Modern made simple. •Birch Lane: Classic style for joyful living. •Joss & Main: The ultimate style edit for home. •Perigold: The destination for luxury home. •Wayfair Professional: A one-stop Pro shop.

analysis_md:
# W — Wayfair Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-17. **In scope** (market cap $13.732B at $107.28, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap). US filer on Form 10-K (FY2025, filed 2026-02-19 per fundamentals.json), USD, no overrides.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The largest pure-play online retailer for the home: furniture, decor, housewares and home improvement sold through Wayfair.com and the specialty / luxury banners (Perigold, Birch Lane, Joss & Main, AllModern), mostly drop-shipped from third-party suppliers and delivered through its CastleGate network for bulky items. Asset model is light on inventory but heavy on logistics, marketing and SBC. Q2 2026 (company release, via search): net revenue $3.5B, +7.5% YoY (U.S. +8.7%, International -1.3%), orders delivered 10.6M (+6.0%), active customers 21.7M (+3.3%), average order value $332, repeat customers 80.2% of orders, adjusted EBITDA $242M, operating cash flow $360M in the quarter — described by the company as its strongest free cash flow since 2020.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $534,000,000; capex $70,000,000; SBC $335,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $129,000,000 = $1.01/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share $1.0078125 on 128,000,000 diluted shares) — the first positive FY in the window.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **-$283,000,000** for FY2025 — it diverges from the conservative figure because FY2025 still carried a -$313,000,000 net loss and a working-capital outflow; the OCF-based conservative figure is the cleaner series and is the one used throughout.
- OE positive **1 of the last 5** fiscal years. Per-year conservative OE/share: FY2021 -$0.34, FY2022 -$12.95, FY2023 -$3.54, FY2024 -$1.23, FY2025 +$1.01. The normalized (3-yr median) base is **-$1.23/share** — the median year is FY2024, deep in the post-COVID trough.
- Balance sheet (latest FY): cash $1,476,000,000, total debt $3,272,000,000, **net debt $1,796,000,000** (basis LongTermDebtNoncurrent+LongTermDebtCurrent), plus lease liabilities $1,025,000,000. Book equity is **-$2,782,000,000** after cumulative losses. The company has been repurchasing convertible notes in 2026 (per its May 2026 8-K and Q2 2026 call reporting) to cut maturities and potential dilution, funded in part by new secured notes — leverage is falling, not gone.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $534,000,000 − prior YTD $177,000,000 + current YTD $308,000,000 = **TTM $665,000,000**
- Capex: FY $70,000,000 − prior YTD $18,000,000 + current YTD $51,000,000 = **TTM $103,000,000**
- SBC: FY $335,000,000 − prior YTD $164,000,000 + current YTD $136,000,000 = **TTM $307,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **131,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $255,000,000 → base OE/share $1.95** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Why TTM over the median: the median (-$1.23/share) averages in the 2023–24 trough (SBC peaked at $605M in FY2023, revenue was still shrinking) and is the distorted base (it is the FY2024 trough year, not a through-cycle average). The TTM legs are internally consistent (OCF rising, SBC falling in absolute dollars: $605M FY2023 → $395M FY2024 → $335M FY2025 → $307M TTM), and fundamentals.json's independent TTM build agrees in substance (TTM revenue $12,904,000,000, +7.46% YoY; TTM operating income $215,000,000). Even so, the TTM base is one inflection, not a through-cycle record — confidence is low and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate, scale without pricing power
Justification: Largest pure-play online home-goods retailer with real scale assets — CastleGate bulky-parcel logistics, a deep third-party supplier/selection network, 21.7M active customers with 80.2% of Q2 2026 orders from repeat customers, and specialty/luxury brands (Perigold +35% in Q2 2026) — but no demonstrated return on capital and no pricing power in the numbers: gross margin has been flat at ~30% for four years (28.0% FY2022, 30.6% FY2023, 30.2% FY2024, 30.2% FY2025, 30.1% TTM in fundamentals.json), book equity is negative (-$2,782M at FY2025) so the roic_proxy series is denominator noise (-49.0% FY2020, +236.1% FY2022, -1.4% FY2025), and conservative owner's earnings were positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years. Consumers face near-zero switching costs against Amazon, Walmart, IKEA and the big-box chains. A 4 gives CAP 7.2 years.
- FOR: Scale pure-play in online home goods ($12,457M FY2025 revenue, 21.7M active customers, repeat customers 80.2% of Q2 2026 orders); CastleGate specialized logistics for bulky / large-parcel delivery — the category generalists handle worst; supplier and selection network plus house / specialty brands (Perigold grew >35% in Q2 2026, specialty brands ~20%) with higher-margin mix; share capture in a fragmented market (Q2 2026 revenue +7.5% YoY, U.S. +8.7%, while the home category was roughly flat-to-down).
- AGAINST: No pricing power — gross margin flat at ~30% FY2023–2025 despite scale gains; promotion- and paid-search-driven demand. No demonstrated returns on capital — negative book equity, OE positive 1/5 years. Near-zero consumer switching costs vs Amazon, Walmart, IKEA, Home Depot / Lowe's. SBC-driven dilution — diluted shares 106M (FY2022) → 128M (FY2025) → 131M (current YTD), +6.5%/yr CAGR, SBC still $307M TTM. Levered and cyclical — net debt $1,796M plus $1,025M leases against a just-positive OE base; demand tracks housing turnover, and imported assortment carries tariff exposure.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-17)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blend is -4.35% — it straddles the post-COVID bust (revenue -10.9% in FY2022, -1.8% FY2023, -1.3% FY2024) and carries the full -5.00pp share-count adjustment on every revenue component, so the default scenario starts (-10.0% / -9.4% / -4.4% / +0.6% / +7.6%) sit below what the company is actually printing now: FY2025 revenue +5.11%, TTM revenue +7.46% (fundamentals.json), Q1 2026 revenue +7%, Q2 2026 +7.5%. Offsets were therefore set to -0.06 / +0.04 / +0.11 / +0.18 / +0.26 against g_base, giving OE/share starts of -10.0% (the engine's floor for the super-bear start) / -0.4% / **+6.7%** / +13.7% / +21.6%: the base start tracks the current revenue print with no margin-expansion credit, the bull starts add operating leverage (SBC already falling in dollars, management guiding toward higher adjusted-EBITDA margins), and the super-bear start replays a 2022-style revenue decline on a levered cost base. Probabilities stay at the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults; OE multipliers stay 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $107.28.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -10.0% | 0.75 | Housing / discretionary downturn replays 2022; OE collapses on the levered, fixed-logistics base | $7.34 | 3.23% |
| Bear | 25% | -0.4% | 0.90 | Revenue stalls, no further margin or SBC progress; dilution eats what growth there is | $12.87 | 3.96% |
| Base | 30% | 6.7% | 1.00 | Current ~7% revenue trajectory holds, OE/share grows with sales and no heroic margin credit | $18.71 | 4.76% |
| Bull | 25% | 13.7% | 1.10 | Share capture compounds, specialty / Perigold mix and SBC discipline add operating leverage | $26.78 | 5.87% |
| Super bull | 10% | 21.6% | 1.25 | Multi-year double-digit compounding with margin expansion toward the company's long-term targets | $40.82 | 7.72% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $20.34 (-81.0% vs price), IV@12% $27.16, IV@10% $34.79, weighted IRR 5.01%, base-case IRR 4.76%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D, bull D — no TIER_BAND). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 1.81%, terminal value 19.2% of IV@15%, scenario spread 5.56x, net debt 7.2x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- The decisive fact: even the super-bull case — a 21.6% OE/share growth start, 1.25x OE — returns only 7.72% at $107.28. No scenario in the set comes within half of the 15% hurdle at this price. The hurdle-clearing price on the weighted case is $20.34.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 10 months ago in the preliminary wording; 9.5 months in the final diagnostics): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, quoted leg-by-leg above.
- **DILUTION** (share count +6.5%/yr): partly mechanical, partly real. Diluted shares rose 106,000,000 (FY2022) → 114,000,000 (FY2023) → 123,000,000 (FY2024) → 128,000,000 (FY2025) → 131,000,000 current YTD, driven by SBC issuance in loss years when buybacks were impossible. The SBC leg behind it is improving in dollars — $605,000,000 (FY2023) → $395,000,000 (FY2024) → $335,000,000 (FY2025) → $307,000,000 TTM — and 2026 convertible repurchases cut potential future dilution, but the count is still rising and the -5.00pp growth adjustment in the blend is earned, not a data error. It is one reason the recalibrated base start (6.7%) sits at, not above, the revenue print.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): resolved — the bridge is non-cash SBC and depreciation, not a tax deposit or a hidden cash one-off. From financials_history.csv: FY2023 net income -$738,000,000 vs OCF +$349,000,000 with SBC $605,000,000 and D&A $417,000,000; FY2024 net income -$492,000,000 vs OCF +$317,000,000 with SBC $395,000,000 and D&A $387,000,000; FY2025 net income -$313,000,000 vs OCF +$534,000,000 with SBC $335,000,000 and D&A $305,000,000. Restructuring charges from the 2024–25 layoff rounds and the Germany exit sit inside the net losses but do not change the bridge's character. OCF adds SBC back as non-cash; the conservative OE deducts it in full, so the divergence makes the base more conservative, not less — and the base is still only $1.95/share.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (base OE yield 1.8%): real and decisive — at $107.28 against $1.95/share of TTM OE, the price is almost entirely a growth-and-margin-expansion claim. Handled by recalibrating growth upward to and beyond the current prints (bull +13.7%, super-bull +21.6%); the tier still lands D by a wide margin, so the flag strengthens the verdict's direction rather than changing it.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 5.6x super-bear IV): real — a business at a profitability inflection on a levered balance sheet has a genuinely wide range. Confidence is capped (set to low, also for the 1/5 positive-OE history), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end; notably the whole spread, $7.34 to $40.82 of IV@15%, sits far below the $107.28 price.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 7.2x normalized OE): stated from the filing — net debt $1,796,000,000 (total debt $3,272,000,000 less cash $1,476,000,000) plus $1,025,000,000 of lease liabilities, against book equity of -$2,782,000,000. The 7.2x multiple uses the engine's normalized-OE denominator and is best read as "leverage is large relative to a just-inflected OE stream": in the bear cases (OE mult 0.75–0.90) there is little residual after logistics capex, which is why bear IVs sit at $7–13. ## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range: F to D, all far below the hurdle.** On the normalized 3-yr median base (-$1.23/share) the preliminary run was Tier F (sub-type sbc_exceeds_cash: on the median window, OCF − capex is positive and SBC consumes it). On the latest-FY base ($1.01/share) the same scenario set would print roughly half the TTM IVs. On the TTM base ($1.95/share) with growth recalibrated to current prints it is Tier D at 5.01% weighted. No defensible base or growth set gets this price near 15%.
- The turnaround itself is not in dispute: revenue has re-accelerated from -1.3% (FY2024) to +5.1% (FY2025) to +7.5% (Q2 2026, U.S. +8.7%), SBC is falling in dollars, OCF is at a post-2020 high, and the company is taking share in a flat category. What is in dispute is the price of that story: $107.28 is ~55x the TTM OE/share and ~1.06x TTM sales for a business whose gross margin has not expanded past ~30% in four years and whose OE was negative in 4 of the last 5 years.
- What would change the tier: OE/share, not revenue. If SBC flattened and OCF margin expanded so TTM OE/share reached roughly $5–6 at the current share count, the same scenario machinery would start printing double-digit IRRs. That is a plausible 2–3 year path — it is just already paid for at this price, with leverage and a housing cycle still to survive.
- Quality note for the file: founder-led, genuinely improving operator, honest capital-return language (management itself calls SBC "a real economic expense" on the Q2 2026 call, per search reporting) — but on this screen quality without OE conversion at the price is a D.
